jobs.title: Associate Director / Director, Customer Program Management, Life Sciences
jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is looking for an Associate Director / Director, Program Management, Life Sciences — a senior operator who will drive the planning, execution, and delivery of therapeutic programs on Lila's platform. This person will provide direct project management leadership to the internal science, engineering, and automation teams developing molecules for our partners, owning timelines, resourcing, and progress tracking across complex, multidisciplinary programs. They will also serve as a senior operational interface with our pharmaceutical and biotech partners, ensuring that deliverables, governance, and communication are running smoothly.

These programs carry significant scientific complexity and commercial stakes. This role requires someone who can drive execution across fast-moving, technically demanding programs from the inside while maintaining the partner-facing judgment and presence to keep external stakeholders informed and aligned.

What You'll Be Building

- Own end-to-end project management for active therapeutic programs, including timeline development, resource coordination, milestone tracking, and dependency management across product, science, machine learning and automation teams

- Drive day-to-day execution discipline; ensuring that internal teams have clear priorities, deliverables, and decision points, and that blockers are identified and resolved quickly

- Manage resource allocation discussions and trade-off decisions across a complex set of priorities (e.g., balancing experiments between AI model training and near-term partnership deliverables)

- Establish and maintain program-level reporting, including status updates, milestone tracking, and resource utilization views for internal leadership and external deliverables

- Proactively identify, communicate, and manage program risks, escalating appropriately and ensuring transparency with scientific and executive leadership

- Structure and facilitate effective internal program meetings, decision forums, and reviews; ensuring the right information reaches the right people at the right time

Partner-Facing Delivery

- Serve as the primary operational interface with partner organizations, coordinating joint governance, managing deliverable timelines, and driving alignment on milestones and expectations

- Translate internal program status into clear, structured updates for external partners, ensuring transparency without overexposing internal complexity

- Support alliance obligations including joint steering committees, milestone reporting, and deliverable handoffs

- Partner closely with scientific and product leadership to ensure that program plans reflect both Lila's platform capabilities and partner-specific program goals and business objectives

Process & Scale

- Lead the development of scalable project management practices, templates, and tools as Lila's partnership portfolio grows

- Help build repeatable operating models for how Lila plans, tracks, and delivers partner programs

What You’ll Need to Succeed

- 8+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry in roles associated with drug discovery or development, project management, or operations

- 5+ years in program management, project management, or a similar cross-functional coordination role with direct responsibility for timelines, resourcing, and tracking

- Demonstrated ability to independently drive execution across complex, multidisciplinary programs with significant scientific and commercial stakes

- Strong understanding of drug discovery and development processes; ability to engage credibly with scientific stakeholders and communicate at a high level across therapeutic and technical domains

- Experience managing programs with external partners, including milestone management, governance, and stakeholder communication

- Outstanding communication skills, with the ability to distill complex scientific and operational information for diverse audiences including executive leadership and external partners

- Proven ability to influence without authority and drive alignment across cross-functional teams

Bonus Points For

- Experience working at or partnering with AI-native or platform-based drug discovery companies

- Experience managing external collaborations in a discovery or preclinical setting (alliance management, CRO/CDMO oversight, or joint research programs)

- Familiarity with project management tools and methodologies (e.g., critical path analysis, scenario planning, resource management, portfolio reporting)

- Familiarity with the rapid evolution of LLMs and AI-driven science platforms and a perspective on how this will impact partnership models in drug discovery

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

International Benefits. Full-time employees outside the U.S. receive a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region. USD salary ranges apply only to U.S.-based positions; international salaries are set to local market.

Expected Base Salary Range
$148,000 — $224,000 USD

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Associate Director / Director, Customer Program Management, Physical Sciences
jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is building a new Customer Delivery & Success function, and we're looking for an Associate Director / Director, Customer Program Management to lead delivery for our physical sciences customer partnerships. In this role, you're bringing LILA's science into the real world with customers. This is a senior, hands-on role that sits at the center of high-value, multi-year customer engagements: you will be the primary face of LILA to the customer, the operational owner of a complex program spanning multiple concurrent projects, and a founding contributor to how LILA delivers for customers as we scale.

This is not a lightweight, account management role. Our engagements are deeply technical and highly consultative, and the customer relies on you to understand where the science is, where the program is headed, and what it will take to get there. You'll coordinate across a wide set of internal teams (e.g., AI/ML researchers, experimentalists, automation and hardware engineers, software, product) while owning the customer relationship end to end and shaping where it grows next.

The role has three core dimensions:

- Customer engagement and growth: serving as the primary conduit to the customer, managing the relationship holistically, and recognizing and shaping opportunities to mature the engagement.

- Program management: driving cross-functional operational excellence in a complex scientific environment so that delivery happens to scope, on time, and with quality.

- Delivery infrastructure: helping stand up a new function by building the processes, tooling, and operating models that define what customer delivery looks like across LILA.

What You'll Be Building

Customer Engagement & Growth

- Intentional Relationship Management : Serve as the primary contact and trusted operational interface for the customer, owning the health and trajectory of the relationship over time.

- Clear & Structured Communication : Translate complex internal program status into clear, structured communication for the customer– surfacing and steering milestones, risks, and decisions.

- Trust-Building Governance : steering committees, milestone reviews, deliverable handoffs, and the difficult conversations (delays, quality incidents, scope changes) that sustain trust through the hard moments.

- Customer Renewal & Expansion : Identify and shape opportunities to grow the engagement, partnering with business development and product to bring them to life.

Program Management

- Operational Excellence: Own end-to-end delivery across multiple concurrent projects under a single partnership timelines, resourcing, milestone tracking, dependency & risk management. Promote a high-performance team environment through operational rigor across the program, coaching the wider team toward practices that outlast any one person.

- Cross-Functional Alignment: Coordinate a cross-functional "team of teams" that speaks different technical languages, keeping everyone aligned on shared objectives and clear on priorities and decision points.

- Shared Truth & Situational Awareness : Structure and run effective program meetings, decision forums, and reporting so the right information reaches the right people at the right time.

- Strategic Judgment: Hold many considerations at once (e.g., customer needs, technical constraints, resourcing, risk) and exercise the judgment to chart a course when there's no obviously right answer, recommending a path forward and knowing when to rethink the approach entirely rather than optimize the current one.

Delivery Infrastructure

- Building for Scale: Help build the operating model for customer delivery at Lila: scalable processes, templates, tooling, and best practices that extend well beyond this single program.

- Setting the Standard : Define what operational excellence and delivery success look like for the function, including the metrics and KPIs worth tracking.

- Servant Leadership: Lead with Lila's broader mission in view and contribute to a founding team of delivery leaders be generous with hard-won lessons, invest in your peers' success, and build the low-visibility shared infrastructure that lifts the whole function rather than only your own program.

What You'll Need to Succeed

- A graduate degree (MS, PhD, or equivalent experience) in a physical science or technical discipline (materials science, chemistry, chemical or mechanical engineering, physics, AI/ML research, or a related field), with enough grounding to engage credibly with scientific and technical stakeholders.

- 8+ years of experience in a technical or scientific industry, with 5+ years in program management, delivery, or a similar cross-functional coordination role carrying direct responsibility for timelines, resourcing, and tracking.

- Demonstrated experience as the primary customer-facing owner of a relationship

- Sound judgment about customer relationship health over time: knowing when to push, when to absorb, when to escalate, and how to deliver hard news in a way that strengthens rather than erodes trust.

- A track record of agency in driving execution across complex, multidisciplinary programs with significant technical and commercial stakes.

- Outstanding communication skills, with the ability to distill complex technical and operational information for diverse audiences, from working scientists to executive leadership to customers.

- Proven ability to influence without authority and drive alignment across cross-functional teams.

- Demonstrated ability to thrive and build amid ambiguity and rapid growth; able to create structure where little exists and to turn one-off solutions into repeatable processes.

Bonus Points For

- Experience at or partnering with AI-native, platform-based, or otherwise technically sophisticated science or technology companies.

- Deep familiarity with R&D workflows (experimental iteration, instrumentation and characterization, data quality, scale-up) across one or more of materials, formulations, energy, semiconductors, or related domains.

- Experience managing external collaborations or partnerships in a discovery or R&D, or technical-delivery setting

- Familiarity with project management methods and tools (e.g., critical path analysis, scenario planning, resource modeling, portfolio reporting).

- Experience with LLMs and point of view on how AI and automation are changing how technical work gets delivered

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

jobs.title: Associate Director / Director, Strategic Finance
jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is looking for an Associate Director / Director, Strategic Finance to join our Strategic Finance team. This role sits at the center of the highest-stakes financial workstreams in the company: structuring the complex, multi-year commercial agreements that underpin Lila's partner revenue, supporting the fundraising activity that fuels our scale-up, and partnering with leadership on revenue forecasting and capital allocation across the business.

You'll operate as the connective tissue between Commercial, Legal, Science, and Finance on live deals, and between the CFO's office and outside investors and counsel on capital raises. The role carries real ownership of the operational workstreams around each deal, including negotiation logistics, diligence coordination, contract lifecycle tracking, and cross-team sequencing, alongside the underlying financial analysis. This is a high-visibility seat with regular exposure to executive, board, and investor-level work, on a small, senior, fast-moving team, based on-site in our Cambridge office.

This role is well-suited to someone with a transactional finance background (banking, corporate development, venture/growth investing, or strategic finance) who is energized by deal complexity, comfortable operating across legal, commercial, and operational workstreams simultaneously, and can bring structure to ambiguity under tight timelines.

What You'll Be Building

- Structure and model economics for complex, multi-year strategic partnerships and commercial agreements with customers, including platform/access fees, usage-based and milestone-gated pricing, royalty and buyout mechanics, and tiered rate cards

- Own the operational cadence of deal execution: track open issues, sequence workstreams, and keep Legal, Commercial, and Science aligned on timelines from term sheet through signature

- Partner with Legal (internal and outside counsel) on contract negotiation and redlines, including IP infringement representations and indemnity bundles, license grant structure, and liability caps

- Build and maintain deal comparables and competitive pricing benchmarks to inform negotiation strategy across customer segments

- Support revenue recognition analysis for multi-element arrangements, including option rights, cost-sharing structures, and milestone-based contracts

- Act as a thought partner and operational point person to Commercial and Science leads throughout deal structuring, from initial pricing frameworks through signed agreement and handoff to delivery teams

- Support end-to-end fundraising processes, including cap table modeling, SAFE conversion mechanics, pro forma ownership analysis, and round structuring

- Coordinate the operational mechanics of a live raise: data room management, diligence request tracking, and sequencing across investors, outside counsel, and internal stakeholders

- Build and maintain investor-facing materials, including data room contents, diligence questionnaire (DDQ) responses, and board/investor decks

- Model dilution scenarios and support negotiation of round terms, including valuation, anchor investor terms, and pro-rata rights

- Build and maintain revenue forecasts by customer segment and product line, partnering with the Commercial team to translate deal-level assumptions and pipeline activity into a company-wide view

- Partner with senior leadership on capital allocation decisions across teams and program areas, weighing scientific priorities, market opportunity, and expected returns

- Develop frameworks and analysis that help leadership compare investment options across programs on a consistent basis

- Serve as a connective point across Finance, Legal, Commercial, and Science, translating between deal economics, contract terms, and operational execution

- Partner with Accounting on revenue recognition treatment and audit support for complex, negotiated contracts

- Build scalable tools, templates, and frameworks (pricing models, deal trackers, financial models) that raise the bar on analytical rigor and deal velocity across the team

- Operate with high ownership in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment; move fast with an 80/20 mindset while knowing when precision matters

What You'll Need to Succeed

- 6-10+ years in investment banking, corporate development, venture capital/growth equity, strategic finance, or a related transactional finance field; startup or scale-up experience strongly preferred

- Demonstrated experience structuring and negotiating complex, multi-year commercial agreements

- Fluency in venture financing mechanics (SAFEs, priced rounds, cap tables, liquidation preferences) and comfort supporting live fundraising processes

- Working knowledge of revenue recognition concepts (ASC 606) and the ability to translate contract terms into financial and accounting outcomes

- Experience building revenue forecasts across multiple segments or product lines, and comfort developing capital allocation recommendations under uncertainty

- Strong financial modeling skills, with the ability to build from scratch in ambiguous, fast-changing situations

- Proven ability to drive cross-functional workstreams and keep Legal, Commercial, and Science aligned on timelines and deliverables

- Clear, direct communicator who can operate cross-functionally with Legal, Commercial, and executive stakeholders, and distill complexity for senior leadership and investors

- Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, or a related field (MBA or CFA a plus but not required)

Bonus Points For

- Prior experience in biotech, pharma, deep tech, or AI-native company environments

- Background in M&A diligence or corporate development transaction support

- Direct experience negotiating contract redlines and familiarity with IP, indemnification, and licensing terms

- Experience in an institutional investing seat (VC, growth equity, or banking coverage of growth-stage companies)

- Experience preparing materials for board or investor audiences

Compensation

jobs.title: Chief of Staff to the CEO
jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences is seeking an experienced Chief of Staff to partner with our Founder and CEO, Geoff von Maltzahn, in advancing the company's strategic and scientific priorities. Lila is building the world's first scientific superintelligence platform, applying AI across the scientific method to accelerate discovery in life, chemistry, and materials science. As the company scales, the Office of the CEO requires a senior operator with real technical depth, ideally someone who has built or led inside a technical organization themselves, able to think alongside the CEO on the company's hardest scientific and strategic questions. This is a support role. It sharpens the CEO's thinking and prep and does not replace the technical judgment of the CTO, CPO, or other technical leaders.

The Chief of Staff will serve as a thought partner to the CEO and a connector across the executive team, helping shape and stress-test the scientific bets the company is making. The role combines strategic counsel, technical judgment, and high-trust communication, and requires sound judgment, technical fluency, and the ability to navigate ambiguity at the pace of an early-stage, science-driven company.

Responsibilities span scientific and strategic decision support, board and investor preparation, executive team alignment, oversight of cross-functional initiatives, and stewardship of the CEO's communications and external engagements. The successful candidate will bring deep technical training and hands-on experience, ideally as a founder or in another highly technical capacity, combined with significant experience in senior strategic roles within technology- or science-driven organizations.

This position is based at Lila's Cambridge headquarters at One Charles Park, in person and onsite with the CEO, with willingness to travel as the role requires.

What You'll Be Building

- Serve as a sounding board for the CEO on the company's hardest scientific bets, from which research directions to pursue to how much weight to put on an early result.

- Pressure-test scientific and technical tradeoffs with the CEO before they reach the executive team or the board. Sharpen the reasoning so the decision that comes out is a better one.

- Work with the strategy function and the technical leadership team to turn the company's hardest scientific questions into clear plans and priorities.

- Prepare the CEO for high-stakes scientific conversations with the board, investors, and outside collaborators. Make sure the reasoning behind each decision holds up under scrutiny.

- Own the prep for board meetings, investor updates, and fundraising. Turn the company's scientific and technical progress into materials that land, and make sure the CEO walks in ready.

- Act as the connective tissue between the CEO, the executive team, and the wider company. Make sure scientific context and decisions move fast and nothing important falls through.

- Drive the hardest calls to closure. Cut through competing priorities to the few decisions that matter, and make sure they stick.

What You'll Need to Succeed

- 8+ years of progressive experience, including time as a founder, Chief of Staff, function head, or senior operator at a high-growth company. You've helped shape hard technical or scientific decisions before, ideally in an AI or science-driven environment.

- A PhD, founding experience at a technical company, or equivalent hands-on training in a scientific or AI domain. You engage with the CEO and the research team as a peer.

- You operate without a playbook. This is the first company of its kind, and fast-scaling labs, an active raise, and genuinely hard problems energize you rather than overwhelm you.

- You bring rigor and follow-through to fast-moving, ambitious teams, moving from strategy to the details without missing a step.

- The instinct to push back. You challenge the CEO and the executive team on priorities, strategy, org design, and execution quality, and you get teams to commit and move.

- High emotional intelligence. You build trust fast across scientists, operators, and executives, and you drive outcomes across a leadership team that doesn't report to you.

- Exceptional communicator. You make complex, technical work legible, and you can draft in another executive's voice, from a board deck to an all-hands.

- You thrive in high-stakes complexity. Fast-scaling labs, an active raise, and tackling genuinely hard problems with smart people energize you.

- High discretion, professionalism, and trustworthiness, commensurate with the access this role carries.

- Onsite at One Charles Park in Cambridge, with availability to travel.

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

International Benefits. Full-time employees outside the U.S. receive a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region. USD salary ranges apply only to U.S.-based positions; international salaries are set to local market.

$250,000 — $350,000 USD

jobs.title: Manager / Senior Manager, Finance, Fixed Asset Accounting
jobs.location: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

As the Fixed Asset Accounting Manager at Lila, you'll play a critical role in building and scaling the Company's fixed asset, lease, and capital project accounting infrastructure during a period of rapid growth and innovation. You will own the end-to-end accounting lifecycle for capital assets—from acquisition and capitalization through depreciation, impairment, retirement, and audit support—while partnering closely with Procurement, Facilities, Lab Operations, and Finance.

This role will be instrumental in establishing best-in-class asset accounting processes, ensuring accurate financial reporting, supporting strategic capital investments, and maintaining compliance with U.S. GAAP. You will help build the operational and accounting foundation that supports Lila's expanding laboratory, facilities, and scientific equipment footprint.

What You'll Be Building

Fixed Asset Accounting & Reporting

- Own the fixed asset accounting function, including capitalization, depreciation, disposals, transfers, impairments, and reconciliations.

- Manage the monthly fixed asset close process and prepare supporting journal entries and account reconciliations.

- Maintain accurate fixed asset records and ensure compliance with capitalization policies and U.S. GAAP.

- Review capital expenditures and determine appropriate accounting treatment.

- Support accounting for laboratory equipment, capital leases, leasehold improvements, construction-in-progress projects, and capital infrastructure investments.

- Maintain asset records necessary to support depreciation calculations and fixed asset reporting.

Asset Governance & Lifecycle Controls

- Partner with Procurement, Facilities, and Lab Operations to ensure complete and accurate asset data is captured during purchasing and onboarding.

- Oversee asset identification and tracking standards, including asset tagging and inventory control processes.

- Maintain accurate records of asset ownership, location, lifecycle status, and supporting documentation.

- Coordinate periodic physical inventories and asset verification procedures and investigate discrepancies.

- Ensure consistency of asset information across ERP, procurement, and asset management systems.

Lease & Capital Project Accounting

- Support accounting for operating and finance leases under ASC 842.

- Maintain lease inventories and support tracking of lease commencement dates, renewal options, expiration dates, and lease modifications.

- Partner with Facilities and Procurement to monitor leasehold improvement projects and capital construction activities.

- Oversee construction-in-progress (CIP) tracking and coordinate timely capitalization upon project completion.

- Assist with technical accounting analyses related to capital assets, lease arrangements, and complex capital projects.

Audit, Compliance & Internal Controls

- Prepare audit schedules and support internal and external audit requests related to fixed assets, leases, and capital projects.

- Maintain audit-ready documentation supporting capitalization, depreciation, asset ownership, and asset disposals.

- Develop and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls related to fixed assets and capital expenditures.

- Ensure compliance with U.S. GAAP and company accounting policies.

Systems & Process Improvement

- Drive improvements in fixed asset accounting processes, automation, and reporting.

- Partner on ERP optimization efforts, including NetSuite fixed asset functionality and reporting enhancements.

- Improve integration between procurement, asset management, lease management, and accounting systems.

- Build scalable processes that support Lila's rapidly growing scientific and facilities infrastructure.

What You’ll Need to Succeed

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.

- 6+ years of accounting experience, including public accounting and/or industry experience

- Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, particularly fixed asset accounting, capitalization, depreciation, impairment, and lease accounting.

- Experience supporting fixed asset accounting in a capital-intensive environment

- Experience with ERP systems (NetSuite preferred)

- Advanced Excel skills and strong analytical capabilities.

- Exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities

- Strong communication skills and ability to partner cross-functionally

- Experience supporting laboratory, manufacturing, research, or facility- intensive operations.

Bonus Points For

- Experience with construction-in-progress (CIP) accounting and capital project accounting.

- Experience working with asset management systems, asset tracking programs, or physical inventory processes.

- Experience supporting external audits and compliance environments.

- Familiarity with barcode, QR, or RFID asset tracking methodologies
